## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One fix is needed before this change meets its own goal: the PR body says this "raises the minimum in the password validators", but the invite validator still accepts 8-character passwords. That leaves one account-creation path below the twelve-character policy. This review found no defect in the signup and reset changes or their tests.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/reset.py:1 — correctness — An invited user who sets an 11-character password such as `"x" * 11` still gets it accepted, because `app/invite.py:1` keeps `MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 8` while this diff raises only `app/signup.py:1` and `app/reset.py:1` to `12`. The PR body says it "raises the minimum in the password validators", and `app/invite.py:4-5` uses the same `len(password) >= MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH` check, so it is one of those validators. Raise `app/invite.py:1` to `12` and update `tests/test_invite.py:6-8` to the same `[0, 8, 11, 12, 13]` / `length >= 12` boundary cases. A better long-term fix is to define the constant in one shared module that all three validators import. — Accounts created through the invite flow can keep passwords of 8–11 characters, so the stated security policy is not enforced on that path and the gap is easy to miss because the other two validators were updated.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- The updated boundary tests in `tests/test_reset.py:6` and `tests/test_signup.py:6` cover 11, 12 and 13, which pins the new `>=` boundary on both sides. They also keep 8 as a case that must now be rejected.

(none)
